name: worst_case_representation_mixing
description: The Randolph-Wegrzycki line brings the Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique from average-case to worst-case instances of Subset Balancing, the family of problems asking for a nonzero coefficient vector c in C^n with c.x = 0 (Subset Sum is C={-1,1}, Equal Subset Sum is C={-1,0,1}). The core new ingredients are (1) mixing dichotomies, which show that if candidate solution pairs do not 'mix' (spread out) across residue classes modulo a random prime, then the instance must have either an unbalanced solution or exponentially many solutions - cases solvable by other methods; (2) coefficient shifting, factoring C as a sumset C1+C2 so that coefficient sets without 0 (C=[+-d]) admit flexible representations; and (3) a near-linear compatibility test that recovers a valid solution pair from a list that may contain invalid 'pseudosolution pairs'. For C=[-d:d], d>1 and C=[+-d], d>2 this yields O(|C|^{(0.5-eps)n}) worst-case time, the first worst-case break of the |C|^{n/2} Meet-in-the-Middle barrier on these coefficient sets. Equal Subset Sum (C=[-1:1]) is improved to O(1.7067^n), but the two natural cases C=[+-1] (Partition/Subset Sum) and C=[+-2] remain unresolved.
worst_case_time: O(|C|^{(0.5 - eps)n}) with a constant eps = eps(C) > 0 depending only on C, for C = [-d:d] (d > 1) and C = [±d] (d > 2); O(1.7067^n) for Equal Subset Sum C = [-1:1]. Baseline Meet-in-the-Middle is O(|C|^{n/2}). The two exceptions C = [±1] (Partition/Subset Sum) and C = [±2] are not improved.
space_complexity: Not the focus of the paper and no explicit worst-case space bound is stated; the algorithms enumerate/filter candidate vector sets of exponential size, so space is at least polynomial-multiple of the filtered list sizes (exponential). [uncertain]
model: Word RAM / circuit RAM with unit-cost operations on input integers (the paper assumes standard integer operations take constant time, reconcilable with a realistic RAM model via O* notation; this follows the Chen-Jin-Randolph-Servedio model).
randomized_or_deterministic: Monte Carlo with one-sided error (never returns false positives); success probability is inverse polynomial and can be amplified to 1 - 2^{-Omega(n)} by repetition.
time_space_tradeoff_curve: Single point per coefficient set; the paper focuses on shaving the exponential time exponent and explicitly does not optimize space or constant factors.
numerical_exponent_and_record_year: Equal Subset Sum (C=[-1:1]): O(1.7067^n), improving the previous O(1.7088^n) (Mucha-Nederlof-Pawlewicz-Wegrzycki, ESA 2019); record year 2025 (arXiv Nov 2025). For general C=[-d:d] and C=[±d] only the symbolic exponent |C|^{0.5-eps} with unspecified constant eps > 0 is given; record year 2025.
problem_variant: Subset Balancing (c.x = 0 for c in C^n), which generalizes Subset Sum/Partition (C = {-1,1}), Equal Subset Sum (C = {-1,0,1}) and average-case Subset Balancing.
applies_to: Worst-case exact Subset Balancing for coefficient sets C = [-d:d] = {-d,...,d} with d > 1 (includes 0) and C = [±d] = {-d,...,-1,1,...,d} with d > 2 (excludes 0). Does not apply to C = [±1] (Partition/Subset Sum) or C = [±2].
coefficient_set: Constant-size coefficient set C subset of Z. Two families: [-d:d] with |C| = 2d+1 and [±d] with |C| = 2d. Results hold for d > 1 ([-d:d]) and d > 2 ([±d]) with a constant eps depending only on C. The unresolved cases are [±1] and [±2].
density_regime: Worst-case / dense arbitrary integer inputs; no density or distributional assumption. (Contrast: the earlier Chen-Jin-Randolph-Servedio result assumed uniformly random inputs from an exponential range.)
solution_regime: General decision/search regime, not a promised numerous-solution (pigeonhole) regime. The mixing dichotomy handles instances that have a single balanced solution by proving that poor mixing forces either an unbalanced solution or exponentially many solutions.
cardinality_constraint: No explicit fixed cardinality constraint, but the algorithm guesses the 'solution profile' (the frequency of each coefficient in C) and separately handles unbalanced profiles vs approximately balanced profiles.
key_technique: Worst-case adaptation of the Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique, combining: (1) mixing dichotomies (poor mixing implies an unbalanced solution or exponentially many solutions); (2) coefficient shifting, expressing C as a sumset C1 + C2 to create flexible representations for coefficient sets without 0; (3) representations admitting pseudosolutions plus compatibility certificates (a sparse-OV-style near-linear compatibility test, generalizing Belova-Chukhin-Kulikov-Mihajlin) to rule out invalid pairs; and (4) a folklore fast algorithm for epsilon-unbalanced instances.
core_idea: The representation technique filters a large ambient set of candidate vectors down to a smaller set Z by keeping only vectors whose dot product with the input equals a fixed random residue r modulo a random prime p, so that any solution pair survives with good probability. This requires candidate pairs to 'mix well' (fall into many residue classes). For worst-case inputs mixing may fail; the mixing dichotomy converts that failure into structure (unbalanced solution or many solutions) solvable by other means, while for well-mixing instances the filtered space drops below |C|^{n/2}, beating Meet-in-the-Middle.
reduction_pipeline: No reduction to an external problem; the method works directly by modular filtering of candidate vector sets. Coefficient shifting is an internal algebraic reduction C = C1 + C2 (e.g. {0,1} + {-3,-2,1,2} = [±3]). The compatibility-certificate subroutine is inspired by a sparse Orthogonal Vectors technique.
constructive_vs_existential: Constructive: the algorithms are fully algorithmic and output a solution.
search_vs_decision_witness: Returns an explicit witness (a nonzero coefficient vector c in C^n with c.x = 0); constructivity is proved, not merely existential.
obstacle_to_2n3: The method only reduces the coefficient base, yielding |C|^{(0.5-eps)n}; it does not approach a 2^{n/3} time bound for {0,1} Subset Sum. Two natural worst-case cases are left unbroken: C = [±1] (Partition/Subset Sum itself) and C = [±2]. Since a faster algorithm for [±1] would imply one for [±2] (by a blow-up self-reduction), the technique as presented cannot reach further until the no-zero coefficient sets are handled. Moreover the 2^{n/3} regime is currently established only for Pigeonhole Equal Subset Sum (a total-search regime with guaranteed many solutions), not for general worst-case Subset Sum.
potential_to_break_mitm: Medium for the general Subset Balancing family (many coefficient sets now broken in the worst case), but low-to-medium for collapsing all the way to 2^{n/3}: C = [±1] and C = [±2] are explicitly named as remaining barriers, and the authors frame the result as strengthening the 'circumstantial case' rather than solving Partition.
barrier_evidence: No proven lower bound rules out beating Meet-in-the-Middle; the hardness is the unproven MITM conjecture. The concrete barrier in this work is the pair of unresolved coefficient sets C = [±1] (Partition/Subset Sum) and C = [±2], with [±1] implying [±2]. SETH gives lower bounds only for the pseudopolynomial regime, not this one. The paper notes that additional insights may be needed if [±2] is genuinely hard.
open_questions: (1) Break the Meet-in-the-Middle barrier in the worst case for C = [±1] (Partition/Subset Sum) and C = [±2]. (2) Optimize the constant eps and the constant/base factors, which the authors deliberately leave unoptimized. (3) Tighten the integration of compatibility certificates with the [-d:d] and [±d] algorithms for further runtime gains. (4) Derive a time-space tradeoff for these worst-case balancing algorithms. (5) Determine whether the representation/mixing framework can yield a single-exponential improvement visible for {0,1} Subset Sum.
conditional_hypothesis: No conditional hypothesis is needed for the upper bounds; they are unconditional. The hardness of the remaining cases rests only on the unproven Meet-in-the-Middle conjecture (whether O(2^{(0.5-eps)n}) worst-case Subset Sum exists). SETH is relevant only to pseudopolynomial lower bounds.
worst_case_vs_average_case_guarantee: Worst-case. This is precisely the advance over Chen-Jin-Randolph-Servedio (SODA 2022), which obtained the same type of improvement only in the average case.
cryptographic_regime: The representation technique originates in knapsack cryptanalysis (Howgrave-Graham-Joux, CRYPTO 2010) and low-density Subset Sum is polytime-solvable; however these worst-case results do not themselves break knapsack cryptosystems, which rely on the average-case low-density regime. No concrete density/sample parameters are given.
pseudopolynomial_interaction: No direct combination with DP/proximity is used or claimed; the paper focuses on the exponential (n exponent) regime. A future interplay with pseudopolynomial methods for dense or small-item regimes is conceivable but not developed. [uncertain]

empirical_evidence: None. This is a theoretical upper-bound result; no benchmarks or experiments are reported.
verification_method: A reader can reproduce the proofs of the main theorems (Theorem 5.1 for C=[-d:d], Theorem 6.1 for C=[±d], d>2, Theorem 7.1 for Equal Subset Sum) and the compatibility-certificate theorem (Theorem 8.1) from the arXiv paper, and verify the entropy-based runtime calculations. Monte Carlo correctness can be checked by implementing the modular-filter algorithm and amplifying the one-sided-error success probability.
